hypothesis: Removing the canonical breakout-onset requirement from the exact v52 HYPE alignment route would expose a repeatable after-cost opportunity.

analysis.finding: The predeclared 20-path reassessment threshold is satisfied at five minutes. Removing the onset gate would have exposed a population with a strongly negative independent mean, negative median, negative largest-winner-removed mean, only two small cost-clearing closes, and no robust favorable excursion. Fifteen- and thirty-minute evidence is also negative. The positive sixty-minute mean is supported by only four resolved paths and reverses to -23.08 bps when its largest winner is removed.
analysis.normal_variance_or_defect: No routing, side, telemetry, or data defect is present in this prefix. The rejected relaxation concerns counterfactual opportunity quality, not a broken live route.
analysis.applicable_market_regime: Observed long-structural HYPE compression and pullback conditions without a fresh canonical breakout onset. No independent short-side onset-relaxation evidence exists in this prefix.
analysis.do_nothing_comparison: Keeping the onset gate avoided 22 independent five-minute candidate paths whose average close remained below the fixed friction hurdle. Removing it is not supported by this evidence.
analysis.selection_risk: The sixty-minute outlier cannot be used to select a holding horizon after outcomes are visible. The frozen live route is not a fixed-horizon counterfactual and no fill is assumed.

decision.recommendation: Keep the exact v52 canonical breakout-onset requirement unchanged.
decision.reason: The distinct current-route relaxation reached its scheduled evidence threshold and failed after estimated friction, across shorter horizons, and under largest-winner sensitivity.
decision.confidence_basis: High confidence in bounded telemetry completeness and causal path construction; medium confidence in the economic conclusion because paths are counterfactual completed-candle observations with a fixed cost hurdle rather than fills; low confidence about future short-side behavior because no comparable short-side sample exists.

reopen_condition: Reopen only for a separately versioned causal mechanism or a materially different predeclared regime window that produces at least 20 independent same-side paths with positive after-cost mean and median, positive largest-winner-removed mean, and nonzero robust-MFE breadth. A technical implementation defect would override this evidence threshold and be investigated immediately.

highest_value_next_investigation.minimum_evidence: At least one attributable eligible signal and one fully resolved lifecycle for each configured side, with exact fees, slippage, funding, stop, opposite-signal, and maximum-hold attribution.
highest_value_next_investigation.reason: The onset-relaxation question is now rejected; exact live translation and both-side economics remain unresolved.

failure_modes_and_falsifiers: An eligible HYPE decision is lost without an explicit action, withholding, conflict, occupancy, staleness, or technical-failure reason.
A bounded-source replay disagrees with the serialized independent path counts or outcomes.
Actual entry and exit costs materially differ from the fixed 13 bps counterfactual hurdle.
A predeclared independent regime window satisfies the reopen condition.
Live side, stop, opposite-signal, or maximum-hold behavior differs from the frozen v52 implementation contract.
limitations: Counterfactual completed-candle paths are not orders, fills, realized PnL, or proof of route profitability.
The 13 bps friction hurdle is a fixed modeled assumption; v52 has no fills yet to validate current HYPE execution costs.
Only the long side reached the one-blocker threshold in this prefix.
Longer horizons are increasingly right-censored and have much smaller independent samples.
This decision rejects only removal of the onset requirement; it does not promote, reject, resize, or retune the existing HYPE route.
